mechanism_narrative: A further decline in WORKPLACES mobility signals weaker commuting and lower midday demand, which reduces incidental retail visits and pulls RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps falling or remains below -8 for four weeks but RETAIL_REC averages higher than the prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility stays elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, more activity is consolidated near home and discretionary shopping shifts toward local or online channels, lowering retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays at or below -15 while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 8
failure_condition: If the RESIDENTIAL-high and TRANSIT-low condition persists for two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not drop relative to the last two-week average, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT above its recent depressed level restores access to commercial districts and increases foot traffic to retail destinations, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points from its prior-week level
failure_condition: If TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points and RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the following month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS mobility diverts discretionary outings toward outdoor recreation and away from indoor shopping, causing RETAIL_REC to weaken over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by 3 points or more week-on-week
failure_condition: If PARKS jumps by at least 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not fall in the subsequent week, this hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC move in opposite directions for two consecutive weeks, households are re-allocating errands away from discretionary shopping; that substitution suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM holds steady or rises while RETAIL_REC also rises over the next month, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continuing decline in WORKPLACES combined with flat TRANSIT indicates persistent remote work and fewer downtown trips, which will keep RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls another 2 points while TRANSIT stays at or below -15
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES weakens further and TRANSIT stays depressed but RETAIL_REC nevertheless rises above its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, falling PARKS and TRANSIT mobility should coincide with lower retail access and fewer discretionary outings, pushing RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT both fall by 2 points or more from their previous-week values
failure_condition: If both PARKS and TRANSIT drop by at least 2 points but RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM together with stable RESIDENTIAL time implies more bundled neighborhood errands and less discretionary shopping elsewhere, which will depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 8
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 with RESIDENTIAL still above 8 but RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next month, the mechanism fails.
